thesis: Persistent positive close-location and eligible-universe dollar-volume pressure that produces muted close-to-open displacement represents absorption; when short residual return turns positive after that stored pressure, the release should continue cross-sectionally.
primitive: Quantiacs daily OHLCV and historical is_liquid only
signal_contract: Daily signed pressure = positive close-location value times positive log dollar-volume-share surprise. Bounded displacement efficiency = abs(close-open log return) divided by same-day high-low range fraction, clipped to [0,1]. Absorption memory is the rolling mean of pressure*(1-efficiency). Base score requires positive absorption memory and a positive 5-day residual return; score magnitude is absorption memory times positive 5-day residual return.
ablation: remove the muted-displacement absorption transform: use rolling positive pressure memory under the same positive 5-day residual-release condition
falsifier: deterministically rotate absorption-memory values across currently eligible identities before applying the same release condition
selection: positive scores, top five, deterministic label tie breaks
allocation: fixed slots min(0.25, 1/K); unused slots cash
cost_hypothesis: Weekly fixed-slot deployment should contain turnover; exact 0/4/8/12% ATR-linked ladder is evaluated without post-result tuning.
failure_mode: daily candle geometry is too noisy, absorption adds nothing beyond signed pressure, or identity rotation preserves the result
stop_rule: freeze if matched ablation or destructive falsifier matches/beats the central parent, or if every valid base cell is below the fixed 1.0 development floor; do not invert, retune, or grid-rescue after observing failure
validation: 2023-2024 is SPENT_DO_NOT_MUTATE and excluded; 2025+ diagnostic and live evidence never drive mutation
contamination_notes: A-M volatility evidence is already observed. frontier_20260913m reserve returns were not observed before this preregistration. No Frontier-N returns were observed before freeze.
